title: A big file a line at a time

terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node make-year.js` writes a year of the logger's readings to `water/year.txt`, about 26 MB. `node try.js --memory=16 count-readings.js water/year.txt` runs your script with 16 MB for its data, as the logger box has.

tasks.title: Count the readings a line at a time
tasks.description:
Write `count-readings.js` so that `node count-readings.js water/june.txt` prints how many readings the log holds:

```
8 readings
```

A reading is a line like `2026-06-14T07:00,north,0`. Blank lines and the logger's notes, the lines that start with `#`, are not readings. The script reads the log a line at a time with `node:readline` over a read stream, and keeps only the count, so a log far bigger than the memory it has still works.

Check runs `count-readings.js` with 16 MB for its data on a log of its own of about 32 MB, and on a short log saved on Windows with a blank line and a note.
nextSteps: Run `node make-year.js`, then try `node try.js --memory=16` with a script that reads `water/year.txt` whole, to see why not.
Open a read stream on the file named after the script's name, and give it to `createInterface`.
Go through the lines with `for await`, adding one for each reading.
Print the count once the loop is over.
hints: `readFile` holds the whole file in memory at once, and splitting it holds every line as well. Neither fits in 16 MB with a 32 MB log.

`createReadStream(file)` from `node:fs` reads a file in small pieces. `createInterface({ input, crlfDelay: Infinity })` from `node:readline` turns the pieces into lines, which `for await` hands you one by one.
`for await (const line of createInterface({ input: createReadStream(file), crlfDelay: Infinity })) { if (line.trim() === '' || line.startsWith('#')) continue; count++ }`.

tasks.title: Add up the litres as the lines go by
tasks.description:
Write `water-year.js` so that `node water-year.js water/june.txt` prints the litres of every reading in the log, added up:

```
Total: 35 litres
```

The litres are the last part of a reading. Blank lines and notes are left out, as before. The script reads a line at a time and keeps only the total so far.

Check runs `water-year.js` with 16 MB for its data on a log of its own of about 32 MB, and on a short log saved on Windows with a blank line and a note.
nextSteps: Read the log a line at a time, as in task 1.
Leave out the lines that are not readings.
Split each reading on its commas and add its litres, as a number, to the total.
Print the total when the loop is over.
hints: Each line is text, so its parts are text too. Adding text to a number joins them.
`line.split(',')` gives the time, the tap and the litres. `Number()` turns the litres into a number you can add.
Inside the loop, after leaving out notes and blank lines: `total += Number(line.split(',')[2])`.

tasks.title: Total each tap
tasks.description:
Imran wants to know which tap uses the most. Write `tap-totals.js` so that `node tap-totals.js water/june.txt` prints one line for each tap in the log with its litres added up, in the order of the taps' names:

```
north: 19 litres
south: 16 litres
```

The tap is the middle part of a reading. Any tap name can turn up, not only these two. The script keeps one total for each tap, never the lines themselves.

Check runs `tap-totals.js` with 16 MB for its data on a log of its own of about 32 MB with three taps, and on a short log saved on Windows.
nextSteps: Read the log a line at a time, leaving out what is not a reading.
Keep the totals in an object or a `Map`, one entry per tap name.
Add each reading's litres to the entry for its tap, making the entry when it is new.
When the loop is over, sort the tap names and print a line for each.
hints: Memory stays flat when you keep only a few numbers, however long the log is. A list of every line grows with it.
A `Map` keeps a value per key: `totals.get(tap)` is `undefined` the first time, so start from 0. The names come out in the order they first turned up, so sort them.
`totals.set(tap, (totals.get(tap) ?? 0) + Number(litres))` in the loop, then `for (const tap of [...totals.keys()].sort())`.
